description:
FOUND s500 (Fable, 2026-09-28) by the review probes for perf round 37 (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s500/review/r500p-float.pl: `1e15-0.5` in a list dropped the statement; r500p-arith.pl row `-1.5 ** 2`).  PRE-EXISTING on main 209e7533.  PPI 1.291.

(a) THE DROP.  `print 1e15-0.5, " ", 2-0.5, " ", 1e3-1, " ", 1.5-0.5;`
    perl: 1e+15 1.5 999 1        PCL: nothing -- "PCL: statement dropped at F line 1: ... -- Bug. Fell through. Missing case: ['Token::Number::Exp<1e15>','Token::Number::Float<-0.5>']"
  PPI's token stream (perl -MPPI; whitespace omitted):
    1.5-0.5   => Number::Float<1.5> Number::Float<-0.5>          <-- expected Float<1.5> Operator<-> Float<0.5>
    1.5 -0.5  => Number::Float<1.5> Number::Float<-0.5>          (same with a space before the minus)
    1.5- 0.5  => Number::Float<1.5> Operator<-> Number::Float<0.5>   (a space AFTER the minus is fine)
    1e3-1     => Number::Exp<1e3> Number<-1>
    0.5-1     => Number::Float<0.5> Number<-1>
    3.-1      => Number::Float<3.> Number<-1>
    1_000.5-1 => Number::Float<1_000.5> Number<-1>
    0x10-1    => Number::Hex<0x10> Number<-1>
    2-0.5     => Number<2> Operator<-> Number::Float<0.5>         (an INTEGER before the minus is lexed right)
    1.5+0.5   => Number::Float<1.5> Operator<+> Number::Float<0.5>  (`+` is fine)
    1.5-$x    => Number::Float<1.5> Operator<-> Symbol<$x>         (a variable after the minus is fine)
  So PPI's plain-integer Number tokenizer consults the previous token before taking a sign, and the Float / Exp / Hex (and presumably Octal / Binary / Version) tokenizers do not.  This is the SIBLING of ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§15 (`)` followed by `-1`), which `Pl::Parser2::_repair_minus_word` / `_repair_glob_multiply` repair on the raw stream with the ONE predicate `_ends_term` -- a Number token of any subclass ends a term, so the repair is: a Number token whose content starts with `-` (or `+`) directly after a token that `_ends_term` is split into Operator<-> + the unsigned Number, and the document is reparsed.  Rule 11: extend the existing repair family (same predicate, same shape), do not write a per-subclass branch.
  Population: grep the corpus for `\d\.\d+-\d`, `\de\d+-\d`, `0x[0-9a-f]+-\d` and read the drop census (`baselines/parse-error-drop-census-s399.tsv` has 0 rows of this message today, so no blessed file hits it, but everyday numeric code -- `2.0-1.0`, `1e-3-1e-4`, `$t*0.5-0.25` -- does).

(b) THE PRECEDENCE SILENT WRONG.  A negative literal at term START before `**`:
    print join(" ", -2**2, -1.5**2, -2.0**2, -1e1**2, -$x**2, (-2)**2, 0-2**2, 1-2**2);
    perl: -4 -2.25 -4 -100 -2.25 4 -4 -3
    PCL : -4  2.25  4  100 -2.25 4 -4 -3       <-- Float and Exp spellings wrong, the integer spelling right
  PPI lexes `-1.5**2` as Number::Float<-1.5> Operator<**> Number<2> (and `-2**2` as Number<-2> ** 2).  Pl/PExpr.pm line ~6530 already splits a NEGATIVE INTEGER literal before `**` ("If a negative literal is followed by **, always split: -3**2 = -(3**2)"); that test must cover EVERY Number subclass (Float, Exp, Hex, Octal, Binary) -- one predicate `is a Number token whose content starts with -`.  Probe the breaking cases: `-2**-1` (perl -0.5), `-2**3**2` (-512), `4 * -2 ** 2` (-16: a negative literal AFTER an operator is a unary minus on the pow too), `-3 ** 0.5`, `2 ** -1.5`, `-1.5 ** 2 + 1`, `-1.5**2` inside a string interpolation `"@{[ -1.5**2 ]}"`, and the list-slice / hash-key spellings `$h{-1.5}` (a key, not an expression) which must NOT change.

WHERE: Pl/Parser2.pm token repairs (`_repair_minus_word` family, ~line 6563) for (a); Pl/PExpr.pm ~6530 for (b).  Rule 13: log the PPI bug in docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md (new section, the dump above, PPI 1.291) + a row in docs/ppi-bug-report.t + a canary in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t, IN THE SAME COMMIT as the workaround.  Guards: Pl/t/minus-word-01.t (the (a) shapes beside the Â§15 rows) + an arithmetic file for (b), inverse-verified.  BAR: Pl/ change => gen bump + artifacts, corpus-diff (list the sites; each a drop today for (a), a silent wrong for (b)), gate-SET scan both populations (a drop stops firing), full sweep.  Everyday-battery shape; a candidate member of the next everyday-singles batch.


=== DONE (s500a, Opus, 2026-09-30) ===
BOTH HALVES WERE ONE PREDICATE.  The §15 workaround `Pl::PExpr::_fix_ppi_negative_number_bug` (cleanup_for_parsing, every parse route) already splits a negative literal into `-` + number when the PREVIOUS token ends a term, and ALWAYS before `**` -- but it tested `ref eq 'PPI::Token::Number'` for the literal AND for the number before it, so only the plain-integer class matched.  Now one predicate `_is_number_token` (any Number subclass: Float Exp Hex Octal Binary Version) answers both, and the split keeps the literal's class.  (Rule 11: the existing sibling repair, not a new document-level pass.)
(a) `1.5-0.5`, `1e15-0.5`, `1e3-1`, `0.5-1`, `3.-1`, `1_000.5-1`, `0x10-1`, `017-1`, `0b11-1`, `1.5 -0.5`, `1e-3-1e-4` no longer DROP the statement; (b) `-1.5**2` -2.25, `-2.0**2` -4, `-1e1**2` -100, `-0x10**2` -256, `-0b11**2` -9, `-017**2` -225, `-1.5 ** 2 + 1` -1.25, `"@{[ -1.5**2 ]}"` -2.25 (all were the positive square).
NEGATIVES unchanged (probed): `$h{-1.5}` a key, `(1.5, -0.5)` two elements, `2 ** -1.5`, `-2**-1`, `-2**3**2`, `4 * -2 ** 2`, `abs -1.5`, `1.5- 0.5`.
FOUND, PRE-EXISTING, filed #2541: a LIST SLICE then adjacent `-N` (`(1)[0]-1`) still drops -- the slice is a PExpr node by the time the split runs.
RULE 13: docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §34 (the dump, PPI 1.291), docs/ppi-bug-report.t rows 84-85 (fail on 1.291), canary Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t -- same commit.
GUARDS: Pl/t/minus-word-01.t rows 21-24 (the three positive rows fail on base; the negatives row passes there).
POPULATION: no FLOAT-N / -FLOAT** site in perl-tests, lib/, cpan-tests or everyday code (grep: only comments) -- emission unchanged over the corpus; gate-SET scan 638 files IDENTICAL.
subject: PPI 1.291: the Number::Float / Number::Exp / Number::Hex tokenizers take a following `-N` as a NEGATIVE NUMBER without looking at the previous token -- (a) `1.5-0.5`, `1e3-1`, `0.5-1`, `0x10-1`, `3.-1` drop the WHOLE STATEMENT (loud: 'Missing case: [Token::Number::Exp<1e15>, Token::Number::Float<-0.5>]'); (b) `-1.5**2` / `-2.0**2` / `-1e1**2` answer +2.25 / 4 / 100 where perl answers -2.25 / -4 / -100 (SILENT WRONG; the INTEGER spelling `-2**2` is already repaired)
